_README: Machine-readable BLOCKED-RUST-EFFECT residue worklist. Built by the round-54 full programmatic residue re-walk (Agent N3). The per-entry staleness arm of scripts/check_audit_coverage_staleness.py reads THIS file (not the prose audit) and FAILs if any `genuinely_missing` entry's `claimed_missing_effect` (resolved through `aliases`) actually exists as a live Rust Effect:: variant AND a wired _ta_dict_to_python_effect bridge arm — i.e. the entry is stale and the audit residue would over-count it. `closed` entries are the historical reclassifications kept for the cron's regression check (they MUST resolve to a live+bridged variant; if one stops resolving, the closure prose itself went stale). One place to update when a residue card is closed: flip its `status` to `closed`, set `resolved_variant`, and sync EOE_PROBE_READINESS_AUDIT.md. See scripts/check_audit_coverage_staleness.py docstring.

_schema.entry: short stable label (matches the audit per-card row)
_schema.claimed_missing_effect: the plan-invented / audit-named Effect the residue row asserts is missing
_schema.aliases: candidate real Rust Effect:: variant names the claimed name could actually be (plan-name -> real-variant resolution; first one present in the live enum wins)
_schema.status: genuinely_missing = audit correctly lists it as BLOCKED-RUST-EFFECT (cron asserts it stays missing); closed = effect arm shipped + bridged, reclassified out (cron asserts it stays resolvable)
_schema.resolved_variant: for closed entries: the live Rust Effect:: variant the effect actually shipped as
_schema.reclassified_to: for closed entries: the residual non-Effect blocker bucket
